newsitem.title: UK: Alliance hopes continue to boost BAe, GEC.
newsitem.headline: Alliance hopes continue to boost BAe, GEC.

text.p: Shares in British Aerospace and General Electric Co Plc (GEC) bucked a market downtrend, adding to Monday's gains in the wake of a weekend press report which raised hopes of a defence alliance between the two giants.
"It is probably something that will happen in the longer term. It's a question of when rather than if," said Zafar Khan, analyst at SocGen.

GEC firmed 1-1/2 pence to 380, while BAe advanced nine pence to 1,177-1/2. BAe was also helped by comments from German defence minister Volker Ruehe that his country was firmly committed to buying 180 Eurofighter aircraft, analysts said.

BAe, which benefited recently from several positive broker notes, rose 22-1/2 pence on Monday after the Sunday Times reported Britain was prepared to drop objections against an alliance between BAe and GEC.
But while analysts see further consolodiation in the European defence industry as inevitable, they do not expect a BAe-GEC link-up soon.

First of all, they expect GEC's new managing director George Simpson, the former BAe deputy chairman, to settle in and weigh all strategic options before trying to strike a deal with his former employer.
Secondly, analysts expect BAe to sit tight while awaiting to see consolidation moves in France, where the government named BAe' partner Lagardere as the preferred buyer for Thomson.
